answers.answer: Two parts. (1) IMPLIED MOVE: 10.22%. First expiry after the 2026-10-01 print is 2026-10-02; spot $1015.80, ATM strike $1015, call mid $52.80, put mid $51.00, straddle $103.80 -> 103.80/1015.80 = 10.22% (the conventional 0.85x adjustment gives ~8.7%). That is a very large binary: MU is priced to move roughly a tenth of its market cap in one session, and the 10-02 chain's ATM IV is 68-70% versus 41-43% on the pre-print 09-21 expiry, so essentially all of that is event premium. (2) HBM4 CONSENSUS: there is NO explicit sell-side consensus figure for HBM4 committed capacity or allocation share, and I am returning null rather than manufacturing one. Published consensus for MU covers revenue, EPS and gross margin only. But you are not without a baseline -- it is a COMPANY baseline, not a Street one, and it is scoreable. On the FQ3 call Micron stated: CY2026 memory production sold out including HBM4; HBM3E and HBM4 both fully booked through calendar 2027 with demand extending into 2028; over $1B of HBM4 revenue already shipped; HBM4 ramping roughly twice as fast as HBM3E; HBM TAM ~40% CAGR to ~$100B by CY2028. That is the bar. On 10-01, a restatement of 'sold out / booked through 2027' is ALREADY PRICED -- it is management's own prior disclosure, not news. A promotion against your low-teens residual requires something strictly beyond it: committed capacity extending into CY2028, a named allocation share or customer count, a wafer-start or bit-share number, or HBM4E pulled forward. Score the delta versus the FQ3 language, not versus the absence of a number. Separately, the FQ4 GUIDE baseline the print gets marked against is $50.0B +/- $1.0B revenue, GAAP GM ~86%, non-GAAP EPS $31.00 +/- $1.00 -- guide, kept separate from consensus and from any beat/miss call, which I will only make on 10-01 with actuals in hand.
